- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is >10% above forecast, model often underreacts — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +1–2% to capture momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility — if last 5 days show high variance, reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
